answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited, stake-backed reputation graph: agents earn trust only through repeated tasks whose outcomes are verified by independent peers, and each new identity must lock a scarce deposit that can be slashed for collusion or fraud. A pearl of reputation cannot simply be copied to a fresh account; trust grows along a vine of costly, corroborated interactions. Sybils can still appear, but to gain influence the attacker must fund many deposits and sustain believable work, making a hollow identity farm expensive and slow.
